source_text: His igitur iustitiae, quas praemisimus, divisionibus explicatis, discutiamus quae sit definitio peccati. Equidem affatim mihi tam philosophantium quam eorum qui catholici fuerunt, quod quaerimus, scripta suppeditant; sed vereor ne refrageris et, si philosophorum ego senatum advocavero, tu continuo sellularios opifices omneque in nos vulgus accendas.
pass_a_gloss: These divisions of justice therefore, which we have sent ahead, having been unfolded, let us shake out what the definition of sin is. Indeed the writings both of those philosophizing and of those who were catholic supply me abundantly what we seek; but I fear lest you resist and, if I shall have called in a senate of philosophers, you immediately kindle the sedentary craftsmen and the whole crowd against us,

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: Now that we have explained these distinctions concerning justice, let us examine the definition of sin. The writings both of philosophers and of people who were catholic supply me abundantly with what we seek. But I am afraid you will object: if I summon a senate of philosophers, you will immediately stir up shopkeepers and the whole populace against us,

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
